A1.justification: Both PDFs describe OmniHuman-1 and are readable throughout, including v1's post-reference figures. However, v3 refers to an audio-ratio study in Supplementary Section 5 that is absent from the supplied PDF, limiting comparison of that study.

before.justification: v1 reports original portrait/body animation benchmarks, visual ablations, and a preference study involving 20 subjects and 50 samples.

after.justification: v3 retains the audio-animation benchmarks and reports additional quantitative training ablations, pose-driven comparisons, and qualitative analyses.

M1.justification: The core MMDiT architecture, condition encoders, reference conditioning, and staged training remain. v3 introduces region-selective CFG for choosing the speaker in Section 4.4. Section 3.4 specifies CFG scale 6.5 without retaining v1's annealing description, although it does not explicitly establish whether annealing was abandoned.

E1.justification: v3 adds actual pose-only/video-driven body-animation evaluation in Table 4, substantially extending evaluation beyond v1's audio-driven experiments. Pose-driving capability was already described in v1. The 18.7K-hour training corpus and existing CelebV-HQ, RAVDESS, and CyberHost audio evaluations remain.

E2.justification: v3 adds DisCo, AnimateAnyone, and standalone MimicMotion alongside CyberHost in the pose-driven comparison, plus a pretrained image-to-video comparator in Figure 3. The existing audio comparator sets remain unchanged, including the DiffGest plus MimicMotion pipeline.

E3.justification: v3 introduces quantitative controls for text-data proportions and modality-training order, and adds AKD to the pose evaluation. It specifies audio 50% and pose 25%, whereas v1 states a final pose ratio of 50%. The audio-ratio summary changes 10/50/100% to 10/50/90%, with text fixed at 90%; its full supplementary protocol is unavailable. These are reported setting changes, without establishing reruns.

E4.justification: v3 Table 1 adds systematic text-data and modality-order ablations across three benchmarks; Figures 3 and 5 add pretrained-model comparisons and hand-trajectory analysis. v1's reference-ratio study of drift in 30-second videos is not reproduced in the supplied v3. The audio-ratio study is summarized, but its referenced supplementary evidence cannot be inspected.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added quantitative tables retain the practice of reporting point estimates.

E6.justification: All numerical scores in v1 Tables 1–2 are retained in v3 Tables 2–3. v3 nevertheless adds substantial results in the training-ablation table and pose benchmark, including OmniHuman FVD 7.3184 and AKD 2.136 in Table 4. These are newly reported comparisons, not improvements over the earlier audio benchmark scores.

T1.justification: The two training principles remain heuristic guidance. Neither version supplies formal theorems, proofs, derivations, or mathematical assumptions that are substantively added, removed, or revised.

C1.justification: The central claims about mixed-condition training, data scaling, and broadly applicable human animation remain. v3 emphasizes audio-driven generation with auxiliary conditions and adds an explicit claim to be the first solution supporting input images with any body proportions and image styles.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations of nonmonotonic lip-sync results, declining image-quality scores as greater adherence to reference images, and the effects of modality order on gesture naturalness. Its new Limitation section identifies uncoordinated motion, unrealistic object interactions, distribution mismatch, and CFG-related overfitting, substantially qualifying the earlier presentation.

D1.justification: v3 newly documents AdamW, learning rate 5e-5, batch size 256, gradient clipping 1.0, weight decay 0.01, 400 A100 GPUs, and approximately 10 days per training phase. It also specifies 25 fps, caption-derived text inputs, and 480P/720P evaluation resolutions. Conversely, v1's explicit Seaweed initialization and flow-matching objective descriptions are omitted.

R1.justification: The related-work survey is largely retained. v3 adds Panda-70M as a filtering reference, removes the standalone classifier-free-guidance and flow-matching references, and adds discussion contrasting its modality order with earlier methods. CyberHost's changed title and publication details refer to the same work.

P1.justification: Existing introduction and method prose is extensively rewritten, the numbered contributions become a narrative paragraph, and the training principles receive clearer separate explanations. The experimental narrative is reorganized to put ablations before baseline comparisons, and a limitations section is added.

P2.justification: v3 substantially reorganizes the displays: it adds quantitative-ablation and pose-comparison tables, adds pretrained-model and trajectory figures, and refines Figure 2. v1's Figure 7 is retained as a smaller Figure 4, while its large ablation displays and post-reference galleries are not included in the supplied v3.

improvement.justification: v1 supports its central training principles mainly through visual ablations and a preference study. v3 adds objective ablations across three benchmarks, explicit modality-order controls, and quantitative pose-driving evidence, substantially strengthening support for the central claims. Training details and specific limitations also improve assessability. The unavailable audio-ratio supplement, omitted reference-drift analysis, and underspecified pose-evaluation protocol reduce completeness, but do not outweigh these gains.
